 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Former NBA star Blake Griffin explains how Oklahoma City fans have no choice but to fund the majority of the Thunder's new arena. 
 The Oklahoma City Thunder winning the 2025 NBA Championship changed the lives of the franchise's supporters.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement After clinching the title, the Thunder ownership has also started building a new arena for the team that will be functional from the 2028-29 NBA season.
 The new arena will reportedly cost around $900 million, but the OKC ownership is also contributing $50 million. What about the remaining $850 million? Well, it will be funded by Oklahoma City taxpayers.
 Blake Griffin explains why Oklahoma City citizens have agreed to pay $850 million towards the new arena
 Former NBA star and OKC native Blake Griffin recently shared his two cents on the funding structure of the team's new arena.
 He explained in detail how the fans have no choice but to pay $850 million out of their pockets.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "It's a great team with a recent championship and a ton of pride. So much pride that the people of Oklahoma voted to pretty much buy the organization a new arena, spending $850 million of taxpayer money while the owners are chipping in $50 million.
 "But what choice do fans really have? They know that the alternative is to lose the team and watch Shai [Gilgeous-Alexander] play basketball for the Wichita Thunder," Griffin said.
 He added, "Oklahoma City has the Thunder because Seattle refused to build the Sonics a new arena, and those taxpayer dollars could go to a lot of things.
 "Oklahoma ranks 45th in starting teacher pay. Which matters to me because both my parents were teachers. And now they're paying for that stadium."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Griffin once again reiterated that NBA teams are taking advantage of fans' love for their franchises. But for the Thunder, the situation is worse.
 "The Oklahoma City Thunder one I think is really bad because not only are they funding $850 million of what's supposed to be a $900 million project, they're going to cover all the cost overruns," he concluded.
 As pointed out earlier by Griffin, the fans have literally no choice, unless they want to risk losing the Thunder franchise to a different city.
